subject: GEOMETRY
pageTitle: The Pythagorean Theorem: Formula, Triples and Examples
description: Use a² + b² = c² to find a hypotenuse or a missing leg, learn the common triples, and avoid the mistake of adding instead of squaring.
caption: The Pythagorean theorem in 7 swipes: when to add, when to subtract, and the triples worth memorizing. Free Geometry study guide at precisstudy.com/geometry (no sign-up).

slides.title: THE THEOREM
lines: a and b are the legs
slides.note: It only works on right triangles. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle.

slides.title: TRIPLES WORTH KNOWING
slides.note: Multiples count too: 6, 8, 10 is just 3, 4, 5 doubled.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Legs are 6 and 8. Find the hypotenuse.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: Hypotenuse is 13 and one leg is 5. Find the other leg.

slides.title: WATCH OUT
points: Square each leg first, then add, then take the square root.
The hypotenuse is always the longest side. If you get a shorter one, recheck.
